newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to Feb 14.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover down in week to Feb 14.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange BSE) reported on Monday a sharp 54 percent drop in its turnover in the week ending February 14 and traders blamed tight liquidity for the plunge.
Total BSE turnover fell to 24.936 million dinars ($4.46 million) in 171 transactions, from 54.323 million dinars in 149 deals a week ago.
The bourse trading in standard financial derivatives remained largely in line with the market performance over last several weeks, traders said.

"The picture only seemed distorted because the total turnover figure for the week ending February 7 included the value of shares sold. They accounted for 25.5 million dinars of the BSE total," a trader told Reuters.

Otherwise, the market struggled with tight liquidity of the banking sector and traders expected liquidity to tighten even more ahead of February 28 when companies and banks are legally obliged to present their annual financial reports.
"Plenty of funds will be withdrawn for the purpose of advance payment of taxes and other contributions. But right now, companies and banks withdraw funds to pay salaries," the trader said.

"The situation becomes impossible. There are so many things ripe for change, but how can you change anything in an economy where not even one million employees finance 1.5 million pensioners, the same number of unemployed and a large state apparatus of around 500,000 people," another trader said.
"Of course there is no money available for this market."
For the week ending February 14, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper traded 132 times for a volume of 16.933 million dinars.
* Treasury bills accounted for 23 deals worth 2.8 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between an annual 331 and 793 percent, with maturity running between 1 and 30 days.
* BSE reported two deals in central bank short-term bonds totalling 1.2 million dinars.
* There was no trade in wheat contracts, certificates of deposit and giro money.
The bourse said Serbia's Commodity Reserve Agency will reopen on Monday the third round of sale of wheat contracts, aimed at raising funds to finance the 1997 wheat crop.
The total size of the new tranche is 148.5 million dinars. The contract's face value remains 9,000 dinars, with 10 tonnes of wheat sold as collateral and a 32 percent discount.
* OTC trade in commercial paper and treasury bills jumped to 33.243 million dinars from 21.09 million a week ago.
* OTC trade in giro money, with banks trading their surplus liquidity, fell to 27.19 million dinars from 30.159 million a week ago. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
